claim: Korean exchanges dominate ZEC trading volume worldwide.
why: Searched CoinGecko's full 82-pair, 48-venue ZEC ticker set (22 Aug 2026): it contains zero KRW pairs and zero Korean venues (Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit, Gopax). Upbit delisted ZEC in September 2019 for FATF compliance and has not relisted it. Publishing a Korean-dominance claim would require a venue breakdown showing Korean exchanges present at all, which does not exist.

claim: 21Shares offers a European exchange-traded ZEC product called AZEC.
why: Checked 21Shares' European product listing page directly: it contains no Zcash product of any kind, under the ticker AZEC or otherwise. No European Zcash ETP was located from any issuer. The brief's premise does not hold and should not be asserted.

claim: Grayscale's Zcash exchange-traded product trades under the ticker ZCH.
why: The SEC 8-K filed 21 August 2026 and the S-3/A Amendment 5 filed the same day both state the trading symbol as ZCSH, not ZCH. Cryptobriefing's secondary reporting used ZCH, but the primary filings settle it: use ZCSH.

claim: Jack Gavigan left the Zcash Foundation in 2023 to found Shielded Labs in Switzerland.
why: Shielded Labs was founded in December 2022 by Jason McGee (forum handle aquietinvestor) as a Swiss association; Gavigan is not listed as a founder. Gavigan instead served as Zcash Foundation Executive Director from early 2021 until 4 March 2025 and remains listed on the Foundation's board page.

claim: Josh Swihart became Electric Coin Company CEO in February 2024.
why: Swihart's appointment as ECC CEO, succeeding Zooko Wilcox, was announced 18 December 2023, not February 2024.

claim: Cypherpunk Technologies is led by executives named Will Wolf and Douglas Moore.
why: No 'Will Wolf' exists at Cypherpunk Technologies. The CEO is Douglas E. Onsi (carried over from predecessor Leap Therapeutics); the Chief Investment Officer is William Patrick McEvoy III, publicly known as Will McEvoy, a Principal at Winklevoss Capital. 'Douglas Moore' in the brief appears to be a garbling of Douglas E. Onsi.

claim: Zcash held a Powers of Tau trusted-setup ceremony in 2022.
why: Zcash's Powers of Tau ceremony completed 13 April 2018 with nearly 90 participants, producing the Sapling parameters. No 2022 Powers of Tau ceremony took place; NU5 and Orchard used the Halo 2 proving system, which needs no trusted setup at all.

claim: Upbit suffered a security hack of its ZEC holdings in 2019.
why: Upbit's 2019 ZEC event was a delisting announced 20 September and effective 30 September 2019, citing FATF privacy-coin guidance, not a security breach. The November 2019 Upbit hack that did occur involved 342,000 ETH, an entirely different asset and event. Do not conflate the two.

claim: Electric Coin Company and the Zcash Foundation conducted staff layoffs in 2023 and 2024.
why: No reporting of ECC or Zcash Foundation layoffs in 2023 or 2024 was located. ECC's Q3 2024 transparency report shows a budget deficit but no staff reductions. The event actually on record is the January 2026 mass resignation of ECC's entire engineering and product team to found ZODL, a separate and later event that should not be described as a layoff.

claim: Pantera Capital and Mike Novogratz were seed investors in the Zcash Company.
why: Neither Pantera Capital, Dan Morehead, Mike Novogratz nor Alan Fairless appears in Electric Coin Company's own published list of the 17 investors in the September 2016 $2M raise. Do not assert Pantera or Novogratz as Zcash seed investors.

claim: Coordinated bot networks are pumping ZEC's social-media volume and price.
why: No Nansen, Arkham, Dune, LunarCrush or Santiment study alleging coordinated inauthentic ZEC accounts could be located anywhere. This is an unevidenced allegation, not a documented finding, and must be omitted or explicitly labelled as unverified rather than stated as fact.

claim: Ninety-nine percent of Zcash Founders Reward withdrawals are linkable on-chain without qualification.
why: The sourceable figure from Kappos et al. (USENIX Security 2018) is narrower: 1,943 of 1,953 (99.5%) of the 250.0001-ZEC-denominated withdrawals already flagged by the founder heuristic also matched a separate 6-to-10-block timing pattern. The unqualified 99.x-percent shorthand overstates the finding; publish it only with the withdrawal-subset qualifier attached.

claim: Taylor Hornby published his own technical write-up of the Orchard counterfeiting bug.
why: Searched defuse.ca and the ZecSec index directly; no post about the Orchard bug exists there, and ZecSec's newest entry predates the discovery (January 2024). If a Hornby-authored write-up exists, it was not located anywhere in this research pass.

claim: Arkham published an on-platform post naming the holder of a $174 million ZEC position.
why: CoinDesk (5 June 2026) quotes Arkham describing an unnamed holder who lost over half the value of a $174M ZEC position, a party distinct from Arthur Hayes. The underlying Arkham post or X thread, the holder's identity, and any exchange or address were not locatable; Arkham's public pages render only via JavaScript and are not extractable without an account.

claim: Grayscale has publicly disclosed the on-chain ZEC address holding the Trust's assets.
why: Checked Grayscale's S-3 (26 Nov 2025), S-3/A (18 Aug 2026) and 10-Q (period ended 30 Jun 2026) directly: all three name Gemini as custodian but none discloses a wallet address or publishes proof-of-reserves. No Grayscale-published ZEC address exists in any filing checked.

claim: ZIP 2006's substantive consensus rules restricting transfers into the Orchard pool are published in full.
why: ZIP 2006, 'Restricting Transfers into the Orchard Pool,' carries status Reserved at zips.z.cash and its substantive text is not published, only a placeholder and a reference to GitHub issue #1305. This is the single largest documentation gap found in this research: the rule sealing a pool holding roughly $1.7B has no public specification text.

claim: Zooko Wilcox was paid $250,000 per month in Electric Coin Company compensation.
why: This figure rests on a single line in one Protos article and has no corroborating primary source such as an ECC transparency report or filing. Treat as low confidence and do not headline it; promoting it would require an independent second source.

claim: Bitwise filed a Zcash exchange-traded fund application with the SEC in January 2026.
why: This is reported by a single low-tier outlet, Daily Hodl, describing an 11-altcoin-ETF filing batch on 2 January 2026, and was not independently verified against SEC EDGAR in this research pass. No 19b-4 filing for any Zcash product was located anywhere.

claim: Anthropic's model called Mythos independently audited Zcash's Orchard circuit after the 2026 bug.
why: Shielded Labs and Cointribune name the auditing model 'Mythos' or 'Claude Mythos,' while Cryptobriefing instead describes Opus 4.8 working 'in collaboration with Mythos.' The three accounts are not consistent with each other and no Anthropic statement confirms a product named Mythos. Treat the product identity as low confidence until Anthropic itself names it.

claim: The Orchard bug was actively exploited and the exploiter is now exiting through the Ironwood migration.
why: This is TechLeaks24's inference (8 Aug 2026), arguing that roughly 1.9M ZEC migrating within two weeks is suspiciously fast, and separately alleging early Claude Opus access by VCs before Hornby. No evidence is offered for either claim, and the migration pace is equally explained by Orchard's exit-only design forcing every legitimate holder to move. Cite only with an explicit speculation label, never as fact.

claim: The identity of GenZcash, the sponsor behind CoinDesk's Encrypted Money at Planetary Scale report, is known.
why: GenZcash is named as sponsor at the top of the CoinDesk Research report published 3 November 2025, but no grant record, corporate registration or confirmed account for GenZcash could be found anywhere. Do not assert on the site that GenZcash is ECC, the Zcash Foundation, ZCG or a Winklevoss entity; there is no evidence for that, and the sponsor's identity is genuinely unknown.

claim: Messari's Zcash report titled Building Encrypted Money at Planetary Scale was a sponsored placement.
why: The Messari report page returned a 403 error on every fetch attempt in this research pass, so its sponsorship status could not be checked directly. Do not claim it was sponsored; the title's similarity to the disclosed-sponsored CoinDesk piece is suggestive but not evidence.

claim: NU6.1 activated on the Zcash mainnet on a specific, independently confirmed calendar date.
why: NU6.1's mainnet activation height, 3,146,400, is confirmed by ZIP 255. The calendar date is not independently confirmed anywhere; z.cash's own NU6.1 upgrade page returned empty on repeated fetches. Arithmetic from NU6's confirmed 23 Nov 2024 date at 75 seconds per block gives approximately 22-24 November 2025, but this must be verified against a block explorer before being published as fact.

claim: The current balance of the NU6 development-fund lockbox is publicly known.
why: No current lockbox balance is published anywhere on electriccoin.co, zfnd.org or z.cash. The only figures available are the one-time 78,750 ZEC NU6.1 disbursement under ZIP 271 and a separate approximately 20,000 ZEC Q2 2026 accrual figure; neither is a running current total.

claim: Grayscale's ZCSH shares began trading on NYSE Arca on 25 August 2026.
why: The 21 August 2026 SEC 8-K states shares are anticipated to begin trading 'on or about August 25, 2026,' subject to regulatory approvals, a date three days after this research's 22 August 2026 cutoff. As of the cutoff the listing had not yet happened and could not be confirmed either way.

claim: ZEC's exact intraday low during the 5 June 2026 crash is established at a single precise price.
why: Sources disagree: The Block reports an intraday figure near $250, BitMEX reports $309, and CoinGecko's daily close shows $389.99. No single authoritative low was established in this research; publish the range, not one number.

claim: The exact calendar date of ZEC's November 2025 cycle-high price is settled beyond dispute.
why: CoinGecko's hourly series puts the $723.43 cycle high at 7 November 2025, 18:00 UTC, while BitMEX's own account puts the same approximate price at 17 November 2025, a ten-day discrepancy on otherwise agreeing prices. Prefer the direct CoinGecko data and note the BitMEX date as an open discrepancy rather than resolving it.

claim: ZODL published its promised post-mortem for the 3 June 2026 Zcash chain halt.
why: The greater-than-four-hour chain halt on 3 June 2026 froze deposits on major exchanges, and ZODL publicly promised a full post-mortem at the time. Whether that post-mortem was ever actually published could not be confirmed in this research pass.

claim: The slogan hashtag ZecToTheMoon is a documented Zcash marketing campaign.
why: No documented campaign, origin or amplifier chain for the phrase '#ZecToTheMoon' was found anywhere in this research pass. It does not meet the bar for the phrase catalogue and must not be published as a real Zcash slogan.

claim: Zcash advocates coined and used the slogan the privacy layer of the internet.
why: No discrete first-party use of 'the privacy layer of the internet' as a Zcash slogan was located. The closest documented relative is cypherpunk.com's own phrasing about advancing technologies that guarantee privacy for humans on the internet, which is not the same phrase and should not be conflated with it.

claim: Zcash has publicly billed itself as the only true private cryptocurrency.
why: No sourced first-party use of 'the only true private cryptocurrency' by Zcash, Electric Coin Company or the Zcash Foundation was located. Comparisons to Monero exist in third-party commentary, but attributing this exact phrase to Zcash as a self-description is not supported.

claim: Zooko Wilcox sold ZEC in order to pay a tax bill.
why: Research 04 section 7 item 10 searched for this specifically and found no source at all. The only Zooko-and-tax item it surfaced is a 2017-era Cointelegraph piece about Snowden and tax evasion as a general property of privacy coins, which is a different subject entirely. Treat the claim as unsourced until a primary quote is produced. HANDOFF-02 section 3 names it as one of the five corrected premises that may appear only in this file, so it is recorded here even though nothing in the package asserts it.
